email.body1:
Taylor, saw FloQast cross $200M ARR on enterprise momentum and the rollout of your auditable AI agents.

Growth that fast usually means more in-market accounts than a sales team can personally touch before the window closes. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for FloQast off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Taylor, quick follow-up for FloQast.

When ARR climbs this fast, board expectations on pipeline tend to jump faster than headcount can. Most managers don't know exactly how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter gets tight.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings your team needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Taylor, last bit of proof for FloQast.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how FloQast's reply rate likely compares to peer fintech teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Taylor, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Hitting $200M ARR keeps a team busy, and timing matters more than any pitch.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of 3 AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to FloQast either way.
